description.narrative: Programme activities intend to support civil society organisations, (women) human rights defenders and other activists to claim the necessary civic space that enables them to operate freely and express their legitimate demands. Interventions include strengthening of protection mechanisms and solidarity networks, and enhancing skills in assembling evidence-based reports to influence the policies at regional, national and international levels. The second line of work ultimately aspires that Kenyan authorities acknowledge the violation of rights of Muslim people and their communities, and take adequate measures for redress of victims and non-repetition of such violations. To that end, civil society organisations and rights holders will be supported in documenting and reporting on human rights violations, and to use that evidence in advocacy and dialogue with relevant duty bearers at local or national level.

The Alliance will work in particular with and for (Women) Human Rights Defenders, including journalists, Muslim communities in Kenya’s Coastal and North-eastern region and victims of human rights violations.

The activity is part of a larger programme implemented by the Strengthening Civil Courage Alliance, consisting of ABAAD – Resource Center for Gender Equality, Amnesty International The Netherlands, DefendDefenders, PAX and their partner networks.

The programme focuses on Kenya’s restricted civic space as well as human rights violations in the context of State security sector operations (counter-terrorism operations). At national level, crackdowns on demonstrations violated the freedoms of expression and assembly. Journalists and human rights defenders, youth and targeted populations have been subject to harassment, intimidation, sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV), negative profiling and extrajudicial killings when investigating and speaking out on corruption and extrajudicial executions as well as on issues like reproductive health and gender-based violence. Kenya’s military involvement in Somalia in 2011, as well as its geographic location has made the country vulnerable to acts of (international) terrorism. To counter this vulnerability, Kenya developed and implements counter terrorism measures. In practice, security operations have been negatively impacting the enjoyment of basic human rights of Muslim communities in the Coast and North-eastern regions. These communities have faced widespread discrimination, lack of economic opportunities, marginalization and ethnic or religious profiling by security forces.

This is a longer term objective. No laws and policies are yet better implemented. Partners in Kenya have, however, been actively engaged in the development of a draft Bill on the criminal prohibition of Enforced Dissaperances (ED) in Kenya (SCS2). This draft Bill not only seeks to define the crime and its penalties but most importantly, it has incorporated provisions that address victims needs such as reparations. This draft Bill is still to be adopted by Parliament.

comment.narrative: The local partner positions herself as a thought and collaborative leader towards (re)formulation and or enforcement of appropriate policies, laws, institutions and cultural norms that touch on the safety, security and well-being of HRDs. Submissions on the Data Protection Bill 2018 were made and review of laws related to the exercise of the Power of mercy under Article 133 of the Constitution. The partner engaged in advocacy at the national and in some instances at the local level.

Among the advocacy intiatives in 2024 were: - A Virtual Consultation meeting between Hon. Rémy Ngoy Lumbu, Chairperson, African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights and Kenya Civil Society Organisations on the right to freedom of expression, assembly and association in light of the June protests;- A statement at ACHPR on the situation of women human rights defenders, - A statement on the situation of human rights defenders at ACHPR;- A Side event at ACHPR on youth led reforms for human rights, governance and justice in Kenya;- A Side event on fostering accountability in Assembly Policing; and - A Side event at ACHPR on combating digital repression.

DefendDefenders joined over 10 other national and international organisations working around HRD protection and media freedom in Kenya, to explore ways on how to better protect at-risk HRDs exiled in Kenya. In partnership with Defenders Coalition–Kenya, DefendDefenders hired a consultant to conduct a campaign dubbed "persecuted4speakingup"

During the 50th UN Human Rights Council meeting in Geneva, 2 Human Rights Defenders (HRDs) from our partner in Kenya held private engagements with representatives from different special mandate holders including on freedom of assembly and association, human rights defenders, expression as well as the OHCHR desk officer in charge of Kenya. The HRDs further engaged diplomatic missions from member and observer states of the Human Rights Council to discuss issues pertinent to the August 2022 elections. Ahead of the elections, there were increased reports of targeted attacks and arrests on HRDs. Our partner intended to highlight the situation of HRDs in-country as well as the climate in the run up to these elections and put the international community.The initiative was implemented as planned and no adjustments required. The international community kept an eye on the elections because of the insightful information shared by the 2 staff members of our in-country partner, as evidenced by the press release issued by Special procedure experts: https://www.ohchr.org/en/press-releases/2022/07/kenya-civic-space-and-respect-fundamental-freedoms-key-peaceful-elections-un. This statement affirms the concerns expressed by the Kenyan HRDs and the need for heightened attention through advocacy and lobbying with the international community because of reported political tensions and violence in the campaign period. These meetings were strategically planned and scheduled by the DefendDefenders UN Representative in Geneva. DefendDefenders is a member of HRC-Net, a network of regional and international human rights organisations engaging with the Human Rights Council where advocacy priorities are shared and supported by all members. This means that because Kenya was a priority of DefendDefenders, HRC Net members amplified this course of action. There is no need to change course or follow-up actions required.
